mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% triggers a preemptive equity risk premium, as investors anticipate future rate hikes, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% in the current month
regime_hint: rising inflation expectations in a tightening cycle
failure_condition: Over a 5-year window, 20-day forward returns do not outperform the risk-free rate by more than 1.5 percentage points during inflation spikes above 0.3%, or the S&P 500 underperforms the Treasury 2-year during such spikes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in PAYEMS labor cost index exceeding 0.5% signals wage pressures that prompt central banks to hold rates steady longer, thereby boosting equity valuations and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by more than 0.5% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: During periods where PAYEMS rises >0.5% for ≥2 months, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is not statistically higher than its mean during neutral labor-cost regimes (Granger causality rejected).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in RSAFS industrial production exceeding 2% indicates weakening domestic demand, which typically precedes equity market corrections; however, in a late-cycle environment, this signal can precede a short-term rebound, producing a positive 20-day forward return for the S&P 500.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls by more than 2% in the current month
regime_hint: near or at peak economic cycle
failure_condition: In late-cycle regimes (as measured by GDP growth > 2%), a >2% RSAFS decline is consistently followed by negative 20-day forward returns with p < 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in INDPRO supply index below 95 triggers a forward discounting of future supply growth, raising the equity risk premium and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below 95 in the current month
failure_condition: Over 100 observations where INDPRO < 95, the 5-day forward return is not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained dual increase in both FEDFUNDS and HOUST (household spending) above their prior month's averages indicates a shift toward accommodative policy and stronger consumer demand, which predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and HOUST both increase from previous month in the same direction
regime_hint: policy divergence: rate easing and rising consumption
failure_condition: During periods where both triggers are met, the 60-day forward return does not exceed the mean of the past 5 such windows by more than 1.0 percentage point.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in UNRATE below 4% combined with a sustained monthly decline in PAYEMS of at least 1% signals deflationary pressure and labor market softening, which can produce a short-term negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% AND PAYEMS falls by ≥1% in the current month
failure_condition: In regimes where UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS falls ≥1% for ≥3 consecutive months, the 20-day forward return remains non-negative over 80% of such windows.

mechanism_narrative: A two-month consecutive decline in GDPC1 personal consumption exceeding 2% creates a forward discounting effect on corporate earnings expectations, resulting in a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls by more than 2% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: During such consumption shocks, the 20-day forward return is not significantly below zero (p > 0.10) in 80% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE rises above 6% for three consecutive months in a period of rising FEDFUNDS, it signals tight labor markets and persistent policy tightening, which can suppress equity valuations and produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 6% for three consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS increases from previous month
regime_hint: highly restrictive labor market with persistent policy stance
failure_condition: During such trigger periods, the 60-day forward return does not fall below the mean of prior 10 windows by more than 0.5 percentage points.
